data.title: PRECIOUS METALS | China's Gold Buying Holds $1 Trillion Trade Surplus in Check
data.description: According to Bloomberg, China's gold imports surged to a record $209 billion so far this year in an unprecedented buying spree that followed top officials' promise to make the country the world's marketplace rather than just its factory. The gold buying is keeping China's $1 trillion trade surplus in check.

data.title: Korean Memory Chip Stocks Fall Premarket Amid AI Concerns
data.description: According to Sina Finance, Korean memory chip stocks fell in premarket trading as the retreat from the AI trade continued, extending Friday’s sharp U.S. stock sell-off. On the Nextrade platform, Samsung Electronics fell 5.6% and SK Hynix dropped 6%. The declines came despite South Korean authorities’ pledge on Sunday to step up efforts to stabilize the market. On Friday, the S&P 500 entered correction territory, the Nasdaq 100 posted its worst weekly performance since March 2020, and the VIX, known as Wall Street’s fear gauge, surged to its highest level since April 2025. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 5.2% on Friday.

data.title: STOCKS | U.S. Valuation Shift Puts QDII Fund Net Values Under Pressure
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, U.S. stocks sold off sharply in the early hours of November 21 (UTC+8), putting pressure on QDII funds as investors favored companies with nearer-term, more predictable cash flows. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.28% and the S&P 500 dropped 3.70%. Nvidia lost 14.01%, while Bloom Energy fell 15.30% and Lumentum declined 13.94%.

Several fund firms said institutions were repricing long-duration assets, including technology stocks, long-term bonds and copper, as they focused more on current cash flow. They identified Anthropic’s November 19 Nasdaq listing as a potential catalyst. The report said the IPO was priced at $83 per share and raised $107.3 billion, surpassing SpaceX to become the largest IPO globally. Fund managers said the shift toward long-duration pricing also reflected sensitivity to rising long-term U.S. Treasury yields and higher discount rates.

The selloff weighed on QDII returns. Through the evening of November 20, the four worst-performing products for the year were Hong Kong-themed funds, each down more than 38%; the report said such funds commonly held U.S. assets. By contrast, U.S. real estate and consumer-focused QDII funds had held up better over the past month. One QDII investment head said the firm had increased holdings in cash-flow-focused and non-AI technology stocks and had added exposure to Hong Kong companies with high dividends and strong cash flow.

data.title: Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners Agrees to Sell StraitNZ to Partners Group
data.description: According to Sina Finance, Morgan Stanley Investment Management said investment funds managed by Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners have signed an agreement to sell StraitNZ, a New Zealand-based integrated transport, logistics and ferry company, to Partners Group on behalf of its clients. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals and other closing conditions.

data.title: European Natural Gas Prices Extend Gains as Cold Weather Forecast Boosts Sentiment
data.description: According to Sina Finance, European natural gas prices rose sharply in Asian morning trading as the latest weather forecasts turned colder. Dutch TTF front-month natural gas futures climbed as much as 8.6% to 96.075 euros per megawatt-hour. Forecasts show temperatures in northwestern Europe next week are expected to be about 5 degrees Celsius below the 30-year average for the same period.

data.title: STOCKS | Roundhill Strategist Says Selloff May Be Nearing End, but Bulls Still Need Proof
data.description: According to Jin10, U.S. stock index futures rebounded Monday after all three major indexes closed in technical correction territory last Friday. U.S. markets were closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, and trading ended early at 1 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time on Friday. Market focus is expected to center on volatile technology stocks as investors assess whether last week's selloff marked a firm market bottom or whether stocks could fall further. Roundhill Chief Investment Strategist Drew Pettit said the broad-based selloff had spread beyond technology, which could be a sign that it was nearing its end. He added that bulls still need to provide sufficient evidence to reverse the pessimism currently dominating the market. Pettit said he believes the market's fundamental bottom is much higher, but that technically, bulls need a series of catalysts to show that the case for long-term earnings growth remains intact.

data.title: AI TRENDS | JPMorgan: Recent Market Pullback Driven Mainly by Deleveraging of AI Trades
data.description: According to Jin10, U.S. stock index futures opened higher in early Asian trading, while JPMorgan analysts said they reiterated their view that the recent pullback in risk assets was mainly driven by deleveraging in AI-related trades amid weak market sentiment, as markets also priced in a more hawkish Federal Reserve policy response. The analysts said they remained confident in the durability of the AI supercycle, supported by lower leverage and improved investor positioning. U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent warned Sunday that the Federal Reserve could harm the U.S. economy by tightening monetary policy too aggressively in response to the latest inflation data, and said the financial system was showing signs of fragility.

data.title: Bessent Leaves Door Open to Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia
data.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent no longer ruled out Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, eight days after demanding an outside CEO, as the stock traded about 48% below its 52-week high. Shares fell 14% Friday to close at $125.53, then rose to $130.01 after hours, according to BeInCrypto. Huang resigned Nov. 12 after reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman U.S. officials suspect of ties to Chinese intelligence. Three days later, Bessent called for a dramatic shake-up and gave Nvidia’s board and lawyers 10 days to answer export-compliance questions. On Sunday, responding to CBS host Margaret Brennan about President Donald Trump’s call for Huang’s reinstatement, Bessent said officials needed to see where responsibility lay; Trump had said two days earlier that Huang should apologize and return. Board chair Harvey Jones said Nov. 17 that the board did not intend to reinstate Huang, hours after Huang said he would return if allowed. Bessent said Treasury still needs answers and wants to know whether Megaspeed was a pass-through company. Nvidia also faces a reported SEC accounting inquiry. Options imply an 11.5% move in either direction by the Nov. 27 expiry, with an estimated range of roughly $115 to $145. TipRanks’ 44 analysts have an average 12-month target of $232.59, about 85% above Friday’s close; 30 rate the stock Buy, 13 Hold and one Sell. The lowest target is $130.
